messages:
maya: Heads-up — thinking through the UX for the automatic fallback/rollout switch. We need a single console path for: 1) choosing degrade mode (soft, hard, sampled fallback), 2) error triggers and thresholds, 3) audit + playback. Wanted to surface some tradeoffs.

chris: +1. Core question: do we expose a binary "auto-fallback on/off" or a policy editor with structured knobs?

maya: I prefer structured knobs. Teams want to tune hysteresis/cooldown and sampling without opening the policy DSL. A single toggle hides too much. :thinking:

linh: Agree. Minimal UI controls: mode selector, traffic % for fallback, cooldown secs, trigger windows (errors / latency / token-drop), and a dry-run preview. Also need a clear indicator of what will be audited.

product_ana: From product: audit must include decision_id + policy_version + raw trigger signals. Customers will ask to replay decisions against deterministic traces. We should show both the human-friendly reason ("latency > 500ms x3") and the raw metrics payload.

chris: Important UX point: when users set traffic % for fallback, default should be small (5%) and a canary ramp option. Avoid immediate 100% switch unless explicitly requested.

maya: +1. Also we need an oscillation guard in UI: if policy flips more than N times in M minutes, we show a recommendation to increase cooldown or widen thresholds.

linh: Draft policy JSON we could expose for advanced users (read-only by default, editable via "advanced"):
```json
{
  "policy_name": "auto-fallback-v1",
  "mode": "soft-rollover",        // options: soft-rollover, hard-switchover, sampled-fallback
  "fallback_traffic_pct": 5,
  "triggers": {
    "error_rate": {"threshold": 0.05, "window_sec": 60},
    "p99_latency_ms": {"threshold": 800, "window_sec": 120}
  },
  "cooldown_sec": 300,
  "hysteresis": {"min_time": 30, "max_flips": 3},
  "audit": {"enabled": true, "sample_rate": 1.0, "retention_days": 90}
}
```

product_ana: Love that. A couple points: 1) audit.sample_rate default 1.0 for fails are OK but we should sample quieter events to avoid costs. 2) retention_days should be editable per org/SLA.

chris: Implementation question: where do we store audit traces? We should emit a structured event per decision: event_type=rollout_decision, decision_id, timestamp, trigger_summary, policy_snapshot, input_metrics, resulting_route. That makes playback deterministic if we include model_version + rng_seed if relevant.

linh: Exactly. Proposed event schema keys: ["decision_id","policy_version","trigger_reason","trigger_values","input_hash","final_action","affected_routes","trace_id"]. Keep payload under 1MB but include pointer to raw metrics blobs if needed.

maya: UI affordances: show a compact timeline in the rollout page with markers for each decision (click to open full trace), and a "replay" button that can re-run the decision logic against stored metric slices. Replay should run in a sandboxed preview mode (no customer traffic change).

product_ana: For enterprise, add an "export audit" button and role-based access for audit logs. Also we need a human-ack override path: "manual cutover" with justification box. That action should create a signed audit entry.

chris: Need to protect against accidental manual flips. Require two-step confirm for >50% traffic or hard-switchover. Also record the operator id and policy diff in the audit entry.

maya: Ops-bot: can you add an example API override we can show in docs?

ops-bot: Sure — sample curl to override a rollout (requires auth and role=ops):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/rollouts/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"decision_id":"auto-2024-07-01-abc","override_action":"route_primary","justify":"customer incident","manual":true}'
```

linh: UX nit: show the policy version diff in the confirmation modal (small summary + link to full JSON) and highlight what changed from last applied snapshot.

product_ana: Telemetry naming idea: rollout.decision (info), rollout.replay (debug), rollout.override (audit), rollout.oscillation (warn). Each should have a severity and retention policy.

chris: Also expose metering: tokens spent during fallback vs primary, so teams can see cost delta and tune fallback_traffic_pct.

maya: Edge case: partial fallback across regions — we need per-region policies or one policy with region overrides. UI should allow scoping: global default + per-region override.

linh: Agree. Add a small map UI with region cards where you can quick-toggle the policy scope.

product_ana: Final ask: add an "explain" view that translates policy conditions into plain english for support/PMs. E.g., "Fallback triggered because p99 in us-west2 exceeded 800ms for 2 consecutive minutes."

chris: Sounds good. Next steps: linch to mockups and a minimal backend event schema (linh/chris). Maya will write the UX acceptance criteria and sample error messages. Ops-bot will create an RFC skeleton doc.

ops-bot: RFC created at https://go/redwood/rfcs/auto-fallback-ui-2024 (draft). :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks all — I'll drop a short rubric for test scenarios (oscillation, partial region fail, noisy signals, replay smoke tests) into the RFC by EOD.

chris: Great, ping me when mockups are up — I'll review the telemetry hooks.

linh: I'll start the event schema PR and include example retention/size estimates.

product_ana: I'll draft the product notes for customers (what to expect when auto-fallback is enabled).

maya: Closing thread — feel free to DM if something urgent pops up. :v:
